issues.legal_issue: A will’s genuineness is established when its execution is proved by reliable evidence and suspicious circumstances surrounding it are satisfactorily explained.
material_facts: The probate proceeding concerned a will whose signature was admitted to be the testator’s, but the objectors alleged that it had been written on a blank paper bearing a signature obtained earlier.
Six people attested the will, and four attesters testified; the court found the attesting and other execution witnesses reliable and found no good reason to reject their evidence.
The testator had been found to be in a sound disposing state of mind, and that finding was not challenged in the appeal before the High Court.

The will made no bequest to one daughter and made substantial bequests to other relatives, but evidence showed that the testator had long intended to benefit his grandson and had discussed not leaving immovable property to that daughter.
Evidence also showed that the testator had asked a lawyer to prepare an earlier draft reflecting that intention, and that he had given or intended to give his daughter money.
issues.conclusion: The will was proved to be genuine, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, a will must satisfy the special requirements of attestation; proof is assessed by the satisfaction of a prudent mind rather than mathematical certainty. As stated in H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.N. Thimmajamma, the propounder bears the onus of proving the will, and proof of testamentary capacity and the testator’s signature may suffice when suspicious circumstances are absent. If suspicious circumstances exist, the propounder must explain them to the court’s satisfaction. An apparently unnatural bequest calls for closer scrutiny, but does not itself invalidate a will; a court must not impose its own standard of conduct on a testator.

rule.if: probate_proceeding_appeals_will_genuineness and testator_capacity_proven and will_signature_proven and will_execution_attested_as_required and execution_witnesses_reliable and (suspicious_circumstances_absent or suspicious_circumstances_explained)

predicates.probate_proceeding_appeals_will_genuinen: The proceeding is an appeal in a probate matter in which the genuineness of a will is contested.
predicates.testator_capacity_proven: Evidence establishes that the testator had testamentary capacity when the will was executed.
predicates.will_signature_proven: The testator’s signature on the will is established.
predicates.will_execution_attested_as_required: Evidence establishes that the will was executed with the required attestation.
predicates.execution_witnesses_reliable: The court finds the witnesses who testify about the will’s execution reliable.
predicates.suspicious_circumstances_absent: No circumstances surrounding the will’s execution raise suspicion about its genuineness.
predicates.suspicious_circumstances_explained: The propounder provides a satisfactory explanation for circumstances that raise suspicion about the will’s genuineness.
predicates.will_proved_genuine: The will is established as genuine.

issues.definition: When a probate appeal challenges a will’s genuineness, the will is established as genuine if the testator’s capacity and signature, the required attestation, and reliable execution evidence are shown, and any suspicious circumstances are absent or satisfactorily explained.
